data_objects.name: multi_score_application_records
data_objects.meaning: Application-level records combining identifiers, optional outcome/holdout fields, two AFT aggregate scores, anonymous AFT and PAC feature families, and five additional score variants.

variables.name: apply_date
variables.meaning: Application calendar date encoded as YYYYMMDD.

variables.name: label
variables.meaning: Nullable outcome field; populated values, if present, use a binary-label role indicated by the name.

variables.name: flag
variables.meaning: Categorical sampling or partition flag; random is an observed value.

variables.name: is_held_out
variables.meaning: Nullable indicator intended to mark held-out records.

variables.name: aft_v4_score
variables.meaning: Aggregate score associated with the AFT v4 feature representation.

variables.name: aft_v4_ee_score
variables.meaning: EE-labeled aggregate score associated with AFT v4.

variables.name: aft_v4_f0 … aft_v4_f44
variables.meaning: Forty-five indexed AFT v4 numeric features. The family mixes score-like values and larger count/day-like values; -1 and values such as 366 appear as explicit numeric codes.

variables.name: pac_v2_x0 … pac_v2_x27
variables.meaning: Twenty-eight indexed PAC v2 numeric features on a score-like scale.

variables.name: scene_id
variables.meaning: Second categorical scene identifier, distinct from scene_code.

structure.description: The table is flat and application-grained. All score and feature families align by rowkey; scene_code and scene_id are separate fields and should not be conflated.

uncertainties: The source does not define the outcome, the score calibration, or the semantics of indexed AFT/PAC features.
Numeric special values inside the AFT family are not documented as missing-value sentinels versus valid codes.
annotation_notes: Blank label or is_held_out cells are missing values, not zeros.
The indexed AFT and PAC columns are grouped because they form regular high-dimensional feature families.
